the change
# log10x-caps.csv — engine route rows, keyed by container.
# Generated from this window; caps are scaled to the engine's 240s reset window.
# the engine acts per container today; per-statement disposition is pending engine work, so these rows route the containers hosting the statements above
cartservice,60000:tier_down:MCP poc_from_local soft
otelcol,200000:tier_down:MCP poc_from_local soft
apply
kubectl -n demo create configmap log10x-caps --from-file=log10x-caps.csv \
  --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n demo rollout restart daemonset tenx-fluentd
undo
kubectl -n demo delete configmap log10x-caps
kubectl -n demo rollout restart daemonset tenx-fluentd

What this plan does not touch: every ERROR and WARN event (6.0K this window) stays on the ingest path in full. Statements routed by action 1 land in your own bucket and come back on demand with their statement identifier as the query key.

How to read this. A statement is one line of code in one of your services, recognised across every line it produced. $ marks a value that varied and was removed. The identifier on each statement is stable across restarts and deployments and works as a query key.

Scope. One hour, analysed in place; no log data left the machine. Figures are this window's arithmetic, not an extrapolation. The re-run after applying is the authoritative measurement.
